Research

Our main research directions overlap. We welcome related questions that connect methods, data and meaningful applications.

1

Data Science

Predictive modelling, data curation and evaluation methods for applied research. We are interested in how data quality, study design and validation affect the conclusions a model can support.

Predictive modellingData qualityModel evaluation

Where we could work together

Research datasets, reproducible analysis and the evaluation of predictive models.

2

Deep Learning

Graph neural networks, transformers, multimodal learning and generative models. We study representations and learning strategies for complex scientific data.

Graph learningTransformersMultimodal learning

Where we could work together

Representation learning, complementary data sources and comparisons with strong baselines.

3

Bioinformatics

Computational analysis of biological sequences and molecular data, including peptide prediction and the identification of functional sequence features.

Biological sequencesPeptide predictionFunctional annotation

Where we could work together

Biological datasets, sequence-based prediction and computational questions supported by experimental context.

4

Health Informatics

Data science and AI applied to health information and clinical questions. Our interests include medical prediction, human–computer interaction and the careful evaluation of technologies for healthcare.

Health dataClinical predictionAI and HCI

Where we could work together

Clinically grounded questions, external validation and evidence synthesis.

5

Computer-aided Drug Design

Molecular property prediction, drug–target modelling and computational approaches to molecular design. Our published work also includes molecular data resources and curation software.

Molecular propertiesDrug–target modellingMolecular design

Where we could work together

Molecular datasets, computational screening and modelling linked to experimental follow-up.
